sources: IRGC spokesman Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi (Fars news agency interview; Tasnim report)
fault_line: Deterrence or bluff -- is Iran really ready to change its nuclear doctrine, or is this a bargaining chip for the talks?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Mohebbi via Fars/Tasnim, carried by Al Jazeera + Iran International, Nov 7] (a) NUCLEAR DOCTRINE: 'If the system concludes that it should move in that direction, we will establish the necessary readiness' -- if Iran's leadership decides to revise its nuclear doctrine, the IRGC will make the necessary preparations. NO decision has been announced; Mohebbi did not say what a revised doctrine would involve. (b) MISSILE RANGE LIFTED: 'This restriction has been lifted for us' -- the self-imposed 2,000 km missile-range limit is lifted, following Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's order that threats be met with an immediate response 'without geographical limits' and to update the military target database. Iran continues to enhance missile range and will unveil 'groundbreaking aerospace achievements' in the event of another conflict. (c) CONTEXT: SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Oct 31 no decision on doctrine change had been made; Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei said Nov 2 Iran remains an NPT member bound by its obligations; the doctrine debate follows US/Israeli strikes on Iranian facilities. The same Mohebbi briefing produced the 260-aircraft claim recorded at 1200-02.
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera liveblog (T2) carries the Fars/Tasnim lines; Iran International (T3) carries the Fars interview with the same quotes; Clash Report, Nukta and vietnam.vn relay the same lines (untiered, attribution only). Fars/Tasnim are NOT in the source registry -- they do not count toward corroboration; the tiered carriers do.
sections.what_disputed: No doctrine change has been announced; Rezaei (Oct 31) and Baghaei (Nov 2) confirm no decision. Mohebbi himself cautioned against treating the range statement as proof of a new operational capability (Daily Flare relay of Tasnim). Trump expressly ruled out nuclear use against Iran on Oct 16 (Newsmax). The White House says Tucker Carlson -- who set Nov 7 as a nuclear-decision deadline -- has 'no insight into military planning' (see watchlist 1700-08).
sections.why_matters: Iran just lifted its own missile-range limit -- and its top general says the nuclear doctrine can change on one order. No decision yet. But the limit is gone.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261107-1200-02 (Mohebbi 260-aircraft claim) -- MISSED CATCH-UP (Clash Report 2026-11-07T09:01:00Z = 13:01 ; vietnam.vn 10:34Z = 14:34 ; Nukta 12:57Z = 16:57 ; zero 'nuclear doctrine'/'doctrine' mentions in any prior Nov 6/7 scan -- grep confirms) -- IRGC spokesman Mohebbi: ready to change nuclear doctrine if ordered; missile-range restriction lifted

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran just lifted its own missile-range limit -- and its top general says the nuclear doctrine can change on one order. No decision yet. But the limit is gone. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deterrence or bluff -- is Iran really ready to change its nuclear doctrine, or is this a bargaining chip for the talks?
